items.q: Tapp, this guy I was telling you, Furman Tapp, he' had about eight. That's who my brother-in-law played the trombone with.

ctx.x: And it was a lot of older guys around there playing, you know. Winstead's Wonders, they called them, about seven or eight pieces, and Howard Jordan's band. He had about 7, or maybe about 10. And Tapp, this guy I was telling you, Furman Tapp, he' had about eight. That's who my brother-in-law played the trombone with. Because Dickie had gone, and he was playing with Tapp for awhile, and they come through and went with Lloyd Scott, and that was Dickie, and Bill Coleman.
